gloss: ability to apply knowledge; practical application skills

definitions.gloss: ability to apply knowledge; practical application skills
definitions.explanation: The capacity to take what one has learned and apply it flexibly to new or different situations. Valued highly in education and the workplace.

examples.japanese: {応用力|おうようりょく}を{身|み}につける。
examples.english: To develop the ability to apply knowledge.

examples.japanese: {基礎|きそ}がしっかりしていれば、{応用力|おうようりょく}は{自然|しぜん}とつく。
examples.english: If you have solid fundamentals, applied skills come naturally.

examples.japanese: この{試験|しけん}は{暗記|あんき}だけでなく{応用力|おうようりょく}も{問|と}われるので、{難|むずか}しい。
examples.english: This exam is difficult because it tests not just memorization but also the ability to apply knowledge.

notes:
Describes the practical ability to adapt and apply learned knowledge to new situations. Contrasts with rote memorization ({暗記|あんき}) and basic knowledge ({基礎力|きそりょく}). A key concept in Japanese education.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {応用力|おうようりょく}を{身|み}につける: to acquire applied skills
- {応用力|おうようりょく}がある: to have good application ability
- {応用力|おうようりょく}を{試|ため}す: to test application ability
- {応用力|おうようりょく}を{問|と}う: to test practical application (said of exams)
- {応用力|おうようりょく}が{高|たか}い: to have strong application skills

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {応用|おうよう}: application — the base noun; refers to applying knowledge or technology in general
- {実践力|じっせんりょく}: practical ability — emphasizes hands-on execution rather than flexible thinking
- {基礎力|きそりょく}: fundamental ability — the complementary concept; solid basic knowledge that supports application

ETYMOLOGY:
{応用|おうよう} (application) + {力|りょく} (power, ability).
